To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the carrot mitochondrial cox1 gene contains two reading frames with different C-terminal extensions and that a COX1 protein is produced from the shorter, unextended reading frame irrespective of the presence or absence of the C-terminal extensions in cox1.

the cox1-2 gene in the carrot mitochondrial type SW3 has a C-terminal 284 amino acid extension that is not translated, that rps7 is co-transcribed with both cox1- 1 and cox1-4, that rps3 and cox1 genes are co-transcribed in the carrot mitochondrial types FG17, FW2 and FW3, that the rps3 and rps7 genes are not co-transcribed in mitotype SW3, and
the cox1 transcript in the SW3 mitotype is edited and contains a C-terminal extension, but the protein is not extended, and that in the FW2 and FW3 mitotypes, the COX1 proteins are unextended.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the presence of a 60 kDa protein in mitochondria irrespective of the presence or absence of a C-terminal COX1 extension in the reading frames.
mitochondrial DNA rearrangements and the expression of mitochondrial genes.
the presence and expression of a 60 kDa cox1 protein in mitochondrion of carrot irrespective of its C-terminal extension.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
a 60 kDa protein is the COX1 product irrespective of the presence or absence of the C-terminal extensions in cox1 reading sequences in carrot mitochondria.
the cox1-2 gene is transcribed in SW and FG mitotypes, but not in FW mitotypes, whereas the cox1 -1 gene is transcribed only in SW mitotypes.
in the carrot SW3 mitochondria, the COX1 protein is translated from the primary transcript of the cox1-2 reading frame and is 284 amino acids long.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the C-terminal extensions are not translated into protein.
the COX1 proteins of the SW3 and FG mitotypes contain the same N-terminal region, but different C-terminal regions.
the C-terminal extension of cox1 is not translated and that the 60 kDa mitochondrial COX1 protein is encoded by the unextended cox1 reading fram.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the presence of C-terminally extended COX1 proteins is not essential for the assembly of the COX1 subunits into a functional complex.
a C-terminal extension of COX1 is not required for its expression in carrot mitochondria.
the COX1 protein of carrot is 60 kDa irrespective of whether the reading frame contains a C-terminal extension or a stop codon.
